ordered.title: The Valve Body / Mechatronic Note - Not Always Full Replacement
ordered.description: Many automatic gearbox issues are valve body or mechatronic unit failures - and these can often be repaired rather than replaced.

blocks.text: 🔧 What Is the Valve Body / Mechatronic Unit?

items: Valve Body - Controls fluid flow to clutch packs. Like the "brain" of the gearbox. Failure signs: harsh shifting, delayed engagement, slipping.
Mechatronic Unit - Integrated valve body + electronics (common in DSG/DCT). Failure signs: same as above + warning lights, limp mode.
Solenoids - Electrically controlled valves within the valve body. Failure signs: individual gear issues, delayed engagement.

blocks.text: When Valve Body Repair Makes Sense

rows: Warning light, code points to solenoid

blocks.text: [EM-QUOTE] based on supplier data. Valve body repair can save thousands.

"About 40% of automatic gearbox 'failures' we see are actually valve body or mechatronic issues - not full gearbox failures. The customer thinks they need a new gearbox, but a £500-£1,000 valve body repair solves the problem. Always get a proper diagnostic before assuming the worst."

Important: If the valve body has failed due to internal debris (from worn clutch packs), the gearbox itself may also be damaged. Always get a full diagnostic before deciding on valve body repair vs full replacement.

blocks.question: How much does automatic gearbox replacement cost? −
blocks.answer: Torque converter automatic £1,000-£4,000 , CVT £1,200-£5,000 , DSG/DCT £1,500-£7,000 . Prices vary by gearbox type, condition, and vehicle.

blocks.question: What's the difference between torque converter, CVT, and DSG? +
blocks.answer: Torque converter - traditional auto, smooth, uses fluid coupling. CVT - uses pulleys and belts, seamless ratio changes. DSG/DCT - dual-clutch, fast shifts, sporty.

blocks.question: Can a valve body issue be repaired without replacing the whole gearbox? +
blocks.answer: Yes - many automatic gearbox issues (harsh shifting, delayed engagement) are valve body or mechatronic issues. Repair costs £400-£1,200 - far less than full replacement.

blocks.question: What are the signs of automatic gearbox failure? +
blocks.answer: Harsh shifting, slipping between gears, delayed engagement, transmission overheating, transmission warning light, whining noise, burning smell, leaking fluid.

blocks.question: How long does automatic gearbox replacement take? +
blocks.answer: Labour typically takes 8-15 hours (1-3 days) . Additional time for sourcing the gearbox. Allow 3-7 days for the complete process.

blocks.question: What warranty comes with an automatic gearbox replacement? +
blocks.answer: Used: 3-6 months. Reconditioned: 6-24 months. New: 12-24 months. Always check the specific terms with your supplier.

blocks.question: Is automatic gearbox replacement more expensive than manual? +
blocks.answer: Yes - automatic gearboxes are more complex, have more components, and require more labour. Typical automatic replacement costs £1,000-£5,000 vs manual £500-£3,000 .

blocks.question: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? +
blocks.answer: Gearbox replacement doesn't require DVLA notification. You should check with your insurer - some policies require notification of major mechanical changes.
